trust.title: What it is, and what it isn't
does: Cite the section of the Act behind every answer
Tell you when a section could not be verified
Point you to the Registrar or a lawyer when a dispute or deadline is involved
doesNot: Give legal advice or represent you
Guess when the Act is silent — it says so

items.q: Which Act does it answer from?
items.a: The one you pick. The Multi-State Act is the default; switch to a state Act from the picker at the top of the app.
Yes. Tap the microphone in the composer and speak. Voice input works in Chrome and Edge.
Conversations stay in your browser so you can reopen them. Questions the assistant was unsure about go to a review queue to improve future answers.
No. It explains cooperative law and cites its sources. For a dispute or a deadline, confirm with the Registrar's office or a lawyer before acting.
English, Hindi, Marathi and Tamil, typed or spoken. The interface, the answers and the glossary all follow the language you pick.

items.q: How current is the text of the Acts?
items.a: The assistant answers from the indexed text of each Act and its rules. The status page shows how many sections are indexed; amendments are added when the operator re-indexes.
Nothing during the pilot. The society and federation plans are indicative and billing is not live; you will be told before anything changes.

items.q: Can my society's own bylaws be included?
items.a: Yes. An administrator can index your registered bylaws so that answers cite them alongside the Act.

sections.heading: What we store
sections.body: Your account (name, email, a salted password hash), your conversations, and any feedback you give on answers. Conversations are also kept in your browser so they open instantly.

sections.heading: Where it goes
sections.body: Questions are answered by a language model running on the operator's own server; nothing is sent to third-party AI services. Questions the assistant was unsure about, and answers you mark as unhelpful, are placed in a review queue that administrators can read to improve the corpus.

sections.heading: Voice
sections.body: Voice input uses your browser's speech recognition, which may send audio to your browser vendor for transcription. Read-aloud uses your device's speech synthesis and sends nothing.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.body: Delete a conversation from the sidebar to remove it from your account. Ask the operator to delete your account entirely.

sections.heading: Information, not advice
sections.body: Sahakar Sahayak explains what cooperative-society law says and cites the sections it relies on. It is not a lawyer and does not give legal advice. For a dispute, a deadline or a penalty, confirm with the Registrar's office or a qualified lawyer before acting.

sections.heading: Accuracy
sections.body: The Acts in the corpus are converted from official PDFs and may contain conversion errors or be out of date after amendments. Every answer shows its sources so you can check the text yourself; unverified citations are flagged.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body: Use the service for lawful purposes related to cooperative societies. Do not attempt to overload the service or access other users' data.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: The service is provided as is, without warranty, and may change or be withdrawn at any time.

guide.intro: Every answer goes through four steps. Watch them in the trace above each reply.

understand.title: Understand
understand.body: Reads the question, detects the language and works out whether it is about membership, meetings, elections, audits, bylaws or a dispute.

search.title: Search
search.body: Looks up the Act you selected, and its rules, for the sections that apply, using the indexed text rather than memory.

verify.title: Verify
verify.body: Checks that each cited section really exists and says what the answer claims. Sections that fail are marked unverified.

draft.title: Draft
draft.body: Writes the answer in your language with numbered citations, and flags disputes or deadlines that need the Registrar or a lawyer.

extra.q: How do I switch the Act it answers from?
extra.a: Use the jurisdiction picker in the top bar (or the chip above the composer on the Ask page). The choice is remembered on this device.

extra.q: Can I rename or pin a conversation?
extra.a: Yes. Open the menu on a conversation in the sidebar to rename, pin, export or delete it. Deleting can be undone for a few seconds.
In this browser and in your account, so they follow you to another device once you sign in. Signing out with 'Also clear this device's history' removes the local copy.
